items.headline: What the FTC Wants to Know About How Airlines Set Fares
items.body: Airline pricing has come under more scrutiny in recent years after Delta disclosed it was using AI to price some fares and a lawsuit was filed against JetBlue, alleging that the company uses personal data to price airfares. The airline industry has said it uses no personal data to determine pricing.

Thailand’s 2032 Tourism Plan Chases Spending, Not Arrivals
items.body: Thailand’s $118 billion goal targets spending rather than arrivals, which have stalled at about 33 million. Rising prices will surely lift revenue regardless, but higher rates aren’t the same as higher value, and the plan has no budget yet for the terminals, marinas and guides needed to attract bigger spenders.

items.headline: Regional Visitors Keep Oman’s Arrivals Steady but Can’t Fill Its Hotels
items.body: Oman’s arrivals have held up this year, but its hotels lost more than a tenth of their guests and revenue as Europeans stayed away. Regional travelers are still arriving but make shorter visits at lower rates.

items.headline: Booking.com Bets It Can Close the Trips That ChatGPT and Gemini Start
items.body: AI may own the start of the trip, but Booking.com is betting trust and payments decide who gets the booking. Its experience with superapps, where daily use never became travel spending, suggests generative chatbots may face the same problem.
